newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT, RUGBY UNION - Chiefs lead Super 12, but Auckland loom.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT, RUGBY UNION - Chiefs lead Super 12, but Auckland loom.

text.p: WELLINGTON, March 10 - The Waikato Chiefs lived up to their name this week when they took the lead in the Super 12 rugby competition with Saturday night's away win against NSW, NZPA reports.
But neither their name nor leadership will mean anything come Saturday when they face defending champions Auckland at their new Albany Stadium.
Just as the Chiefs did, Auckland scored a vital away win, 24-15, against Free State at Bloemfontein in their second match.
The third New Zealand team playing away, the Otago Highlanders, managed a bonus point from their high-scoring match although losing 75-43, against last year's competition finalists Natal in Durban.
Despite the 32-point loss Otago scored six tries but lost two over the line when flanker Lio Falaniko and winger Jeff Wilson lost the ball as they stretched out for the touchdown.

But the highlight of the match was the record 50 points scored by Free State import Gavin Lawless from four tries, nine conversions and four penalties. The remarkable feat included 13 successes from 13 shots at goal.
"It was amazing, it was his day," Otago coach Glenn Ross said later.

Ross said it was difficult for his young team to match Natal though he was delighted with their six tries against the well-balanced side that contained some powerful runners in both the backs and forwards.
Natal's rugby strength is spread throughout the team -- from the tall lineout men such as Mark Andrews to a hard-driving pack and powerful running backs.
The side made at least six substitutions while Otago were struggling in the Durban heat and were without their stable inside combination of Stu Forster and Simon Culhane, both injured.
Otago's next match is against Transvaal at Johannesburg's Ellis Park early on Saturday, New Zealand time.
Auckland Blues reject and Counties captain Errol Brain scored the winning try a minute from the end to give the Chiefs a 33-26 win against NSW.

Waikato led 17-9 at halftime following two fine tries by winger Eric Rush, but allowed their opponents to come back and level 26-26 through tries by fullback Matt Burke and front rower Richard Harry before pulling away in the end.
They lead the competition with eight points (not including this morning's Transvaal-ACT match in Johannesburg) followed by Auckland and Northern Transvaal on seven and then Natal on five.
Auckland were never in danger of losing against Free State. They could have captain Zinzan Brooke back in the side on Saturday after injury.
Joeli Vidiri and Ofisa Tonu'u scored a try each.
At home, the Canterbury Crusaders brushed off the Hurricanes 19-17 on Friday. Canterbury play NSW in Sydney this Friday night and Wellington meet Northern Transvaal in New Plymouth on Saturday.
In the other matches Free State host Queensland early on Sunday, New Zealand time, and Natal meet ACT at home early on Monday.
